questions.prompt:
The chemical reaction between calcium carbonate and hydrochloric acid can be represented by the following equation: CaCO3 + 2HC1  →   CaCl2 + CO2 + H20 The carbon dioxide gas (CO2) produced by this reaction can be collected and its volume measured. The following graph represents the volume of carbon dioxide produced over a time period from 0 to 270 seconds when some solid calcium carbonate is reacted with an excess amount of hydrochloric acid.  After how many seconds, from the start of the reaction, had half of the original amount of calcium carbonate reacted?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch122","id":"e344-image1"}]}]
questions.explanation: The final CO2 volume is about40mL;half is20mL,read at about60seconds. This follows1:1CaCO3:CO2stoichiometry with excess acid.
